sources.density_kg_m3: typical value (ledger RCK-001, RCK-086): where the primary tables list the rock, Daly, Manger & Clark 1966 (GSA Memoir 97, Density of rocks) and Manger 1963 (USGS Bulletin 1144-E), the value lies in their measured range; the Telford, Geldart & Sheriff 1990 and Schön 2015 tables cited at stage 1 were not read; rounded to 10 kg/m³; set in P1-12; reviewed in P1-07 against the rock map and meridian cross-sections of pipeline_quick_16k and kept (STATUS.md, P1-07)
sources.erodibility: judgment, relative to granite: strong and fine, though it parts on cleavage; bedrock ranked by rock strength: river incision scales roughly with tensile strength^-2 (Sklar & Dietrich 2001, Geology 29(12):1087–1090) and lithologic K contrasts span orders of magnitude (Stock & Montgomery 1999, JGR 104(B3):4983–4993); the strength-based contrast is compressed to its square root, so bedrock spans about 0.3–4; set in P1-12; reviewed in P1-07 against the rock map and meridian cross-sections of pipeline_quick_16k and kept (STATUS.md, P1-07)
sources.diffusivity: judgment, relative to granite: makes thin, platy rubble; hillslope transport coefficient D of Roering, Kirchner & Dietrich 1999 (WRR 35(3):853–870), used as a linear creep multiplier and scaled by how readily the rock makes mobile soil (soil production function, Heimsath et al. 1997, Nature 388:358–361): loose and friable classes 2–5, soft sedimentary 1.2–2, crystalline 0.5–1; set in P1-12; reviewed in P1-07 against the rock map and meridian cross-sections of pipeline_quick_16k and kept (STATUS.md, P1-07)
sources.vanilla_fallback: P1-28 (Ben, decisions log 2026-10-01): deepslate stands in for the class: metamorphosed shale: dark grey, finely foliated. The MIC rock-tag README's stand-in was minecraft:smooth_basalt; a pack's fallback tags are read first and override this

notes: Slate: the lowest grade of the pelite sequence (slate, phyllite, schist, gneiss).
